messages:
maya: Short thread to lock a long-term routing + tenancy roadmap for the architecture review. Key asks: primitive policy DSL, canary gates, tenancy lanes (latency vs cost), cross-region fallback behavior, and clear owners/launch gates. Can owners land a draft by EOD Fri?

sam: +1. Propose we standardize on 5 small primitives so runtime can evaluate routing decisions without special-casing: lane_id, residency_constraint, fallback_priority, model_variant_constraints, quality_budget_pct. Keep it executable (YAML/JSON).

jana: From customer interviews: three archetypes to map to lanes: Enterprise (pinned region + legal residency + SLA), Scaleups (latency-sensitive, dedicated capacity optional), Startups (cost-first, quantized OK). I'll add contract phrasing for each.

rolf: Ops hard stop: do not run pinned-region canaries without per-tenant telemetry and an automated eviction playbook. Pre-canary probes: per-tenant p50/p95/p99, eviction_rate, kv_cache_hit_rate, capacity_headroom. If any probe missing -> block canary. Also add automatic fallback when eviction_rate > 0.3% over 10m. :no_entry:

ben: For prioritization we'll use a weighted matrix: customer_impact x2, dev_effort, infra_risk, compliance_need. I'll sketch and score initial asks. Can someone own the sheet?

sam: Draft policy snippet (toy):
```
lane_id: enterprise-gold
residency_constraint: region(eu-west-1) # hard
fallback_priority:
  - regional_affinity
  - shared_pool
model_variant_constraints:
  quant_ok: true
  f16_ok: false
quality_budget_pct: 2
rollout_phases: [ff_canary, small_ab, gradual_ramp]
warmup_window_seconds: 600
```
Runtime must evaluate model_variant_constraints and pick a compatible artifact at route time. Also include quality_guard referencing an eval_suite id.

sonja: Billing note: tag every routed request with lane_id so we can attribute costs. Lane-specific rate_limit and billing_tag required to protect shared infra and surface delta to customers.

eli: SRE note: cross-region fallback tends to spike p99 due to cold KV caches and model loads. Suggest staged traffic shifts + KV warmup windows and a quality_delta_pct check during each ramp step. Example schedule: 10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100%, with evaluation windows and rollback on quality_budget or latency breach.

nina: Product/opportunity note: customers will trade cost vs latency. We should present 3 standard lane packages in the deck with clear cutoffs and pricing implications. I'll draft the TL;DR slide.

ben: I'll own the prioritization matrix and add example scores for 8 asks; will share link in the doc. Weighting: customer_impact*2, then subtract ops_mitigation_cost.

rolf: Runbook snippet to include in the doc: pre-canary checklist CLI commands, automated probe queries, and an emergency evacuation playbook. Example rule: if eviction_rate > 0.3% for 10m -> trigger autoscale_burst, route new sessions to fallback_lane, and page SRE.

sam: Also adding a "quality_degradation_pct" field so rollout tooling can compute acceptance. e.g., quality_degradation_pct: 3 means canary allowed to degrade up to 3% vs baseline on eval suite.

deploy-bot: created doc https://redwood.internal/docs/platform/routing-tenancy-roadmap-4278901234 and branch routing/roadmap-4278901234

taylor: I'll build a 3-slide review: TL;DR lanes & customer mapping, policy primitives & sample YAML, gating matrix + prioritization heatmap. Meeting time Thursday 11am?

maya: Thursday 11am works. Owners: Sam (policy + examples), Rolf (telemetry & runbooks), Jana (customer mapping & contract wording), Ben (prioritization matrix), Sonja (billing implications). Please add notes to the doc by EOD Wed so I can synth for the review.

nina: One more: include a short migration path section for existing customers (how to move from shared to affinity or pinned lanes) and outline any contractual changes.

eli: I'll attach SRE tests (k6 snippets + probe queries) to validate warmup and fallback behavior before canary. Also include expected p99 delta graphs for cross-region failovers.

maya: Thanks all. Add PRs to the branch and we'll lock the launch gates during the review. :sparkles:
